categories.label: Filing Formalities
categories.prompt: Assess Form 28 for this SLP (Civil): court and jurisdiction caption, party positions, the petition body, mandatory declarations, grounds, prayers, and any supporting affidavit this task names. Decide only the objection in this message. Do not score other Form 28 points, other categories, or legal merit.

categories.label: Advocate's Check List
categories.prompt: Assess the Advocate's Check List and the Advocate-on-Record's certificate on this filing, including the signature block. Decide only the objection in this message. Do not score sibling defects in this area.

categories.label: Listing Proforma
categories.prompt: Assess the Listing Proforma (Proforma for First Listing) that accompanies the filing. Decide only whether the columns or particulars named in this task are duly filled. Do not score other listing fields unless this task names them.

categories.label: Petition Presentation
categories.prompt: Assess the form of the petition: paper, spacing, font, margins, numbering, signatures and endorsements. Decide only the objection in the user message. Do not score sibling defects in this area.

categories.label: Applications
categories.prompt: Assess interlocutory or miscellaneous applications named in this task (condonation, substitution, caveat, permission to appear). Decide only the objection in this message. Do not score sibling defects in this area.

categories.label: Annexures
categories.prompt: Assess the annexures: markings, true copies, order, and match to the Index or List of Dates. Decide only the objection in this message. Do not score sibling defects in this area.

categories.label: Parties and Cause Title
categories.prompt: Assess the cause title, Memo of Parties, and party particulars named in this task. Decide only the objection in this message. Do not score sibling defects in this area.

categories.label: Drafting and Execution Dates
categories.prompt: Assess the drafting date of the petition relative to filing, the supporting affidavit and the Vakalatnama. Decide only the objection in this message. Do not score sibling defects in this area.

categories.label: Index and Paper Book
categories.prompt: Assess the common index, running pagination, and Part I / Part II (or volume) arrangement of the paper book. Decide only the objection in this message. Do not score sibling defects in this area.

categories.label: Limitation
categories.prompt: Assess the Office Report on Limitation and any condonation of delay for a time-barred petition named in this task. Decide only the objection in this message. Do not score sibling defects in this area.

categories.label: Affidavit
categories.prompt: Assess the supporting affidavit named in this task: presence, form, swearing, exhibits and blanks. Decide only the objection in this message. Do not score sibling defects in this area.

categories.label: Translations
categories.prompt: Assess translations of vernacular documents, official translation or exemption, and translated powers of attorney. Decide only the objection in this message. Do not score sibling defects in this area.

categories.label: Vakalatnama
categories.prompt: Assess the Vakalatnama: execution, acceptance, executant particulars and related endorsements. Decide only the objection in this message. Do not score sibling defects in this area.

categories.label: Memo of Appearance
categories.prompt: Assess the Memo of Appearance named in this task. Decide only the objection in this message. Do not score sibling defects in this area.

categories.label: List of Dates
categories.prompt: Assess the List of Dates and Events named in this task. Decide only the objection in this message. Do not score sibling defects in this area.

defects.defect: The Appeal is not accompanied by the Certified copy of the impugned order passed by the Armed Forces Tribunal
defects.requirement: A statutory appeal under the Armed Forces Tribunal Act must include a certified copy of the impugned judgment or order under Supreme Court Circular F.No.4/Judl./2026 read with Order XIX Rules 3(2) and 40 of the Supreme Court Rules, 2013. Section 31 of the Armed Forces Tribunal Act separately governs leave to appeal; Section 30 does not itself prescribe the certified-copy requirement.
defects.trigger_words: ARMED FORCES TRIBUNAL; Certified to be true copy; Certified Copy; O.A. No.; Original Application No.; PRINCIPAL BENCH; REGIONAL BENCH
where_to_look: Impugned Order: certification of the Armed Forces Tribunal's order
The endorsement on the order such as "Certified to be true copy" or "Certified Copy", with the copying section's stamp, seal and date of issue.
A valid copy is the Tribunal's own order, headed "ARMED FORCES TRIBUNAL" with its O.A. number, bearing that certification.
The order under appeal, matched to the Tribunal, case number and date stated in the Synopsis and List of Dates, not an order of another forum.
how_to_cure: Option for the User to upload the certified copy of the impugned order passed by the Armed Forces Tribunal.

If the copy filed is a plain, downloaded or uncertified copy: Option for the User to upload and replace the impugned order with a corrected version, namely the certified copy issued by the Armed Forces Tribunal.

Option for the User to mark this defect as complete if the filing is not an appeal against an order of the Armed Forces Tribunal, or the certified copy is already filed at another page of the case file.
defects.applicable_rule: Order XIX Rules 3(2) and 40, Supreme Court Rules, 2013; Section 31, Armed Forces Tribunal Act, 2007
defects.location_source: Supreme Court Circular F.No.4/Judl./2026 dated 20 March 2026; Supreme Court Rules, 2013, Order XIX Rules 3(2) and 40; Armed Forces Tribunal Act, 2007, Sections 30-31

Verification — Test this requirement: A statutory appeal under the Armed Forces Tribunal Act must include a certified copy of the impugned judgment or order under Supreme Court Circular F.No.4/Judl./2026 read with Order XIX Rules 3(2) and 40 of the Supreme Court Rules, 2013. defects.defect: The present petition is being filed after the expiry of the prescribed period of thirty days from the date of the dismissal order.
defects.requirement: Under Order XVI Rule 4(1) of the Rules, a petition praying that an appeal dismissed for default of appearance be restored may be presented only within thirty days of the order of dismissal.
defects.trigger_words: dismissed for default; default of appearance; dismissed for non-prosecution; restoration of the appeal; Order XVI Rule 4; Date of filing; recall the order
where_to_look: Main Petition: date of the dismissal order and the date of filing
Record of Proceedings: order dismissing the appeal for default
The date at the head of the dismissal order in the Record of Proceedings, the date below the prayer of the restoration petition, and any delay stated in the Office Report on Limitation.
A valid filing falls within thirty days of the dismissal order; count the days from the order's date to the date of filing.
The restoration petition and the dismissal order that bear this appeal's Supreme Court case number, not orders passed in other matters.
Supreme Court Registry filing/refiling history or the relevant Registry order: use authoritative presentation dates and any period actually allowed; do not use a drafting date as proof of filing.
Return needs_review when the governing period or an authoritative date required for the calculation is unavailable.
how_to_cure: Prompt the User to confirm whether the petition for restoration is being filed beyond thirty days from the date of the dismissal order. If yes:         1. option for Jubeex to auto-draft an application for condonation of delay in filing the restoration petition.
2. Option for the User to upload the application for condonation of delay in filing the restoration petition.
defects.location_source: Page 82 of the PDF Court Processes Handbook.pdf
defects.notes:
Order XVI Rule 4 (1) - An appellant whose appeal has been dismissed for default of appearance may, within thirty days of the order, present a petition praying that the appeal may be restored and the Court may, after giving notice of
such application to the respondent who has entered appearance in the appeal, restore the appeal if good and
sufficient cause is shown, putting the appellant on terms as to costs or otherwise as it thinks fit, or pass such other order as the circumstances of the case and the ends of justice may require.

defects.notes:
Section 11. Appointment of arbitrators.

Section 11 (4) If the appointment procedure in sub-section (3) applies and—
(a) a party fails to appoint an arbitrator within thirty days from the receipt of a request to do so from the other party; or (b) the two appointed arbitrators fail to agree on the third arbitrator within thirty days from the date of their appointment, the appointment shall be made, upon request of a party, by [the Supreme Court or, as the case may be,the High Court or any person or institution designated by such Court];

Section 11 (5) Failing any agreement referred to in sub-section (2), in an arbitration with a sole arbitrator, if the parties fail to agree on the arbitrator within thirty days from receipt of a request by one party from the other party to so agree the appointment shall be made, upon request of a party, by [the Supreme Court or, as the case may be, the High Court or any person or institution designated by such Court].
Section 11 (6) Where, under an appointment procedure agreed upon by the parties -

(a) a party fails to act as required under that procedure; or
(b) the parties, or the two appointed arbitrators, fail to reach an agreement expected of them under that procedure; or
(c) a person, including an institution, fails to perform any function entrusted to him or it under that procedure,
a party may request [the Supreme Court or, as the case may be, the High Court or any person or institution designated by such Court] to take the necessary measure, unless the agreement on the appointment procedure provides other means for securing the appointment.

Compliant — Return Compliant only when affirmative evidence establishes every element of the Requirement across its complete relevant scope. defects.applicable_rule: Order XIX Rule 6 of the Rules
defects.location_source: Page 64 of the PDFCourt Processes Handbook.pdf
defects.notes:
Order XIX Rule 6 applies to specified categories of certificate appeals and contempt appeals which, upon registration, are placed before the Supreme Court for ex parte preliminary hearing. At this stage, the Court may summarily dismiss the appeal, direct issuance of notice to the necessary parties, or pass such other orders as it deems fit. The categories of appeals covered are:

(i) Appeals against a judgment, decree or final order of a High Court summarily dismissing an appeal or other proceeding.

(ii) Certificate appeals where the High Court has granted a certificate under Article 134A of the Constitution, of the nature referred to in Article 132(1) (appeals involving a substantial question of law as to the interpretation of the Constitution) or Article 133(1) (civil appeals involving a substantial question of law of general importance requiring decision by the Supreme Court), or under any other provision of law, without recording reasons or grounds for granting the certificate.

(iii) Appeals under Section 19(1)(b) of the Contempt of Courts Act, 1971, i.e., appeals to the Supreme Court as of right from an order or decision of a Bench of a High Court in the exercise of its contempt jurisdiction.

defects.notes:
Appeals arising under the Advocates Act would ordinarily be filed as Civil Appeals. However, where the challenge is against an interim order passed during proceedings before the court below, the appropriate mode of challenge may be an SLP, rather than a Civil Appeal.

Note to Tech: Train the Agent to identify what order is actually being challenged from the impugned judgment/order. The Agent should determine whether the challenge is against:

a) the final judgment/order in the proceedings; or
b) an interim order passed during the proceedings.

Based on this determination, the Agent should identify whether the matter is being filed under the appropriate main category (Civil Appeal or SLP). Where the selected category appears inconsistent with the nature of the order being challenged, the Agent should caution the user and provide an appropriate advisory before proceeding with the filing.

defects.requirement: Where an appeal falls under Order XX Rule 5(1) of the Supreme Court Rules, 2013, it must be accompanied by a certified copy of the judgment or order of the court immediately below, or an uncertified copy affirmed by affidavit as a true copy. Order XX Rule 5(1) covers (i) appeals against a judgment, final order or sentence of a High Court summarily dismissing a criminal appeal or other criminal proceeding; (ii) certificate appeals where the High Court has granted a certificate under Article 134A in respect of an appeal under Article 132(1) or Article 134(1)(c), or under any other provision of law, without recording reasons or grounds for granting the certificate; and (iii) appeals under Section 19(1)(b) of the Contempt of Courts Act, 1971, against an order or decision of a Bench of a High Court in the exercise of its contempt jurisdiction.

The judgment of the court from which the High Court's decision arose, such as the Trial Court or Sessions Court, not the High Court's impugned judgment itself.

defects.notes:
Order XX Rule 5(1) applies to specified categories of criminal certificate appeals and contempt appeals which, upon registration, are placed before the Supreme Court for ex parte preliminary hearing.The categories of appeals covered are:

(i) Appeals against a judgment, final order or sentence of a High Court summarily dismissing a criminal appeal or other criminal proceeding.

(ii) Certificate appeals where the High Court has granted a certificate under Article 134A of the Constitution, of the nature referred to in Article 132(1) (appeals involving a substantial question of law as to the interpretation of the Constitution) or Article 134(1)(c) (criminal appeals certified by the High Court as fit for appeal to the Supreme Court), or under any other provision of law, without recording reasons or grounds for granting the certificate.

(iii) Appeals under Section 19(1)(b) of the Contempt of Courts Act, 1971, i.e., appeals to the Supreme Court as of right from an order or decision of a Bench of a High Court in the exercise of its contempt jurisdiction.

defects.notes:
The Affidavit accompanying the Petition must be duly attested/notarised. The Affidavit should contain the prescribed verification of the facts stated therein, the required paragraphs as per the prescribed format, the relevant page numbers corresponding to the Synopsis and the LOD filed, a statement confirming that the Annexures are true copies of the respective documents, and reference to the Interlocutory Applications filed along with the Main Petition, wherever applicable.

Duly Attested Meaning:- The Affidavit must be notarised and the corresponding entry must be made in the Notary’s register. The Affidavit should bear the prescribed notarial stamp/seal, including the registration/serial number (Need to check for square stamp). The deponent must also be duly identified before the Notary, ordinarily by an Advocate. Where the deponent appears personally without an Advocate identifying them, the Notary should record the mode of identification, such as identification through an identity document.

Where the deponent is not a resident of the city in which the Affidavit has been notarised, the Affidavit should contain the requisite statement/paragraph regarding this circumstance. The Affidavit should also contain the appropriate verification stating that the facts mentioned therein are true and correct to the best of the deponent’s knowledge and belief.

Order XVI Rule 4- Hearing of Appeals                                                                                             (1)  An appellant whose appeal has been dismissed for default of appearance may, within thirty days of the order, present a petition praying that the appeal may be restored and the Court may, after giving notice of such application to the respondent who has entered appearance in the appeal, restore the appeal if good and sufficient cause is shown, putting the appellant on terms as to costs or otherwise as it thinks fit, or pass such other order as the circumstances of the case and the ends of justice may require.
(2) Where an appeal is heard ex-parte and Judgment is pronounced against the respondent, he may apply to the Court to re-hear the appeal, and if he satisfies the Court that the appeal was set down ex-parte against him without notice to him or that he was prevented by sufficient cause from appearing when the appeal was called on for hearing the Court may re-hear the appeal on such terms as to costs or otherwise as it thinks fit to impose upon him.                                                                                      Order XII Rule 3- Judgments, Decrees And Orders                                                                           (3) Subject to the provisions contained in Order XLVII o f these rules, a judgment pronounced by the Court or by a majority of the Court or by a dissenting Judge in open Court shall not afterwards be altered or added to, save for the purpose of correcting a clerical or arithmetical mistake or an error arising trom any accidental slip or omission.

defects.notes:
Order VIII Rule 6 (3) Where a document is found to be defective, the said document shall, after notice to the party filing the same, be placed before the Registrar. The Registrar may, by an order in writing, decline to receive the document if, in his opinion, the mandatory requirements of the rules are not satisfied. Where, however, the 
defect noticed is formal, the Registrar may allow the party to rectify the same in his presence; but, in other cases, he may require the party to obtain an order from the Court permitting the party to rectify the same and for this purpose may allow to the party concerned, such time as may be necessary but not exceeding 28 days in aggregate.
                                                                                   
Order VIII Rule 6 (4) - Where the party fails to take any steps for the removal of the defect within the time fixed for the same by the Registrar, the Registrar may, for reasons to be recorded in writing, decline to register the document.

defects.notes:
ORDER XLVII - REVIEW
                                                                                                                                                       1.The Court may review its judgment or order, but no application for review will be entertained in a civil proceeding except on the ground mentioned in Order XLVII, rule I of the Code, and in a criminal proceeding except on the ground of an error apparent on the face of the record. The application for review shall be accompanied by a certificate of the Advocate on Record certifying that it is the first application for review and is based on the grounds admissible under the Rules.                                                                                                                                              2. An application for review shall be by a petition, and shall be filed within thirty days from the date of  the judgment or order sought to be reviewed. It shall set out clearly the grounds for review.                                                                                                                                                   3. Unless otherwise ordered by the Court an application for review shall be disposed of by circulation without any oral arguments, but the petitioner may supplement his petition by additional written arguments. The Court may either dismiss the petition or direct notice to the opposite party. An application for review shall as far as practicable be circulated to the same Judge or Bench of Judges that delivered the judgment or order sought to be reviewed.                                                                                                                                                                                   4. Where on an application for review the Court reverses or modifies its former decision in the case on the 
ground of mistake of law or fact, the Court, may, if it thinks fit in the interests of justice to do so, direct the
 refund to the petitioner of the court-fee paid on the application in whole or in part, as it may think fit.                                                                                                       5. Where an application for review of any judgment and order has been made and disposed of, no further 
application for review shall be entertained in the same matter.

Review the complete covered sequence and identify the first break in pagination, chronology, numbering or annexure order.

Defect — Return Defect when applicability is clear and the available relevant evidence positively establishes: Papers of the SLP not arranged in the following order: (i) List of dates; (ii) Certified copies of the judgment and order against which leave is sought; (iii) Special leave petition in Form No. 28; (iv) Appendix containing relevant statutory provisions; (v) Annexures (with page numbers) A complete relevant page/section suffices for a local defect despite unavailable unrelated material. Identify the document, page/section and decisive evidence.

Compliant — Return Compliant only when affirmative evidence establishes every element of the Requirement across its complete relevant scope. Verify every covered page, item, annexure or execution block; a compliant sample is insufficient.

Need Review — Return Need Review only for material uncertainty preventing this decision: necessary evidence is absent/illegible, applicability is unresolved, or controlling evidence conflicts. Inspect supplied material first; name the exact missing/conflicting evidence and why it is decisive. Do not claim a supplied excerpt is unavailable. Do not use Need Review because unrelated pages are missing, the whole file is unavailable, a keyword search failed, or relevant evidence already establishes Defect or Compliant.

N/A — Return N/A only when evidence affirmatively establishes that the filing is outside the petition/special-category scope. Missing evidence or uncertain applicability is not N/A.

Evidence — For D-177, record the document/page, applicability, decisive quote/visual observation, and any comparison or calculation. Do not infer facts.

1.1. Prompt the User to provide details of whether any earlier SLP was filed against the impugned judgment/order and, if so, the result thereof, and option for Jubeex to draft and incorporate the required statement in the Petition.

2.1Option for Jubeex to auto-draft the affidavit accompanying the SLP incorporating the required affirmation with an option for the User to review and edit the draft. Prompt the User to get the affidavit duly sworn and provide an option to upload the duly sworn affidavit with Jubeex.

Legal-source gate — This obligation is marked unverified. Until a current authoritative source confirms it and its applicability, return Need Review rather than Defect or Compliant; record the source once verified.

Inspection — Inspect: Annexures, Main Petition. Focus on: Main Petition: date and nature of the underlying criminal proceeding, the relief sought, and whether the matter invokes Section 482 CrPC or Section 528 BNSS. Annexures: complete FIR and the High Court quashing order, matched by FIR number, police station, case number, parties, and date. Identify the document by its heading, cause title, case number, date and parties, not merely its database label or index reference.

Verification — Test this requirement: determine from a current Supreme Court rule, checklist, or circular whether the FIR and/or quashing order must accompany this filing, and determine whether Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 or Section 528 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 governs the underlying proceeding. Do not retroactively replace the CrPC provision in a 2022 direction without transitional analysis. Use Trigger Words only as locators; inspect supplied material and context before deciding. For a missing-item check, reconcile the complete relevant manifest/index with the actual documents; an index mention is not presence, and an unsuccessful search of partial material is not absence.

Defect — Return Defect when applicability is clear and the available relevant evidence positively establishes: Copy of FIR/Quashing order under Section 528 Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023 is not filed For absence, examine the complete relevant set and expected location; a partial excerpt or failed search alone is insufficient. Apply this outcome only after the Legal-source gate has been satisfied; otherwise return Need Review. A complete relevant page/section suffices for a local defect despite unavailable unrelated material. Identify the document, page/section and decisive evidence.

Compliant — Return Compliant only when affirmative evidence establishes every element of the Requirement across its complete relevant scope. Confirm the actual item, not merely an index entry or reference. Apply this outcome only after the Legal-source gate has been satisfied; otherwise return Need Review.

Inspect supplied material first; name the exact missing/conflicting evidence and why it is decisive. Do not claim a supplied excerpt is unavailable. Do not use Need Review because unrelated pages are missing, the whole file is unavailable, a keyword search failed, or relevant evidence already establishes Defect or Compliant. This is also the required result while the Legal-source gate remains unsatisfied.

N/A — Return N/A only when evidence affirmatively establishes that the filing is outside the petition/special-category scope or that a factual condition activating the Requirement does not arise. Missing evidence or uncertain applicability is not N/A.

defects.defect: Where the number of accused is more than one, the affidavit fails to state that, no bail application has been moved by any of the co-accused persons and, if such an application has been moved, it's details fail to provide the Serial No. for the accused persons
defects.requirement: Where there is more than one accused, the Affidavit must state that no bail application has been moved by any co-accused and, if one has been moved, its details must give the Serial No. of the accused.
defects.trigger_words: co-accused; Serial No.; Sl. No.; S. No.; Name of Accused; no bail application
where_to_look: Affidavit: Serial No. of each co-accused whose bail application was moved
Main Petition: number of accused in the case
The co-accused statement in the Affidavit, often a table with columns "Serial No.", "Name of Accused", "Date of Application", "Case Number", "Date of order" and "Bench".
Each listed co-accused application must carry a Serial No.; a row that shows the other columns but no Serial No. leaves it blank.
The Affidavit filed in this matter under its Supreme Court cause title, as distinct from the bail history narrated in the Main Petition.
how_to_cure: 1. Disclosure of Bail Applications by Co-Accused

1.1. Option for Jubeex to auto-draft the affidavit stating whether any bail application has been moved by any of the co-accused persons, with an option for the User to review and edit it; prompt the User to get the affidavit duly sworn and provide an option to upload the sworn affidavit drafted by Jubeex.
1.2. Option for the User to upload the duly sworn affidavit with Jubeex.
2. Particulars of Bail Applications by Co-Accused

2.1. Prompt the User to provide the prescribed particulars of any bail application moved by the co-accused—Serial No., Name of Accused, Date of Application (if known), Case Number, Date of Order, and Bench, and option for Jubeex to fill the relevant portion of the affidavit.
2.2. Option for the User to add and edit the particulars with Jubeex.
[YOU CAN ALSO PERHAPS INCLUDE DETAILS OF SIMILAR MATTER IN THE L/P]

Applicability — Apply this check only when the filing type falls within: SLP (Criminal)/Writ Petition (Criminal)/Criminal Appeal. It is further limited to the special category: Bail Applications/Bail Matters. Establish each stated trigger from the relevant document; trigger words alone do not establish applicability.

Legal-source gate — This obligation is marked unverified. Until a current authoritative source confirms it and its applicability, return Need Review rather than Defect or Compliant; record the source once verified.

Inspection — Inspect: Affidavit, Main Petition. Focus on: Affidavit: Serial No. of each co-accused whose bail application was moved Main Petition: number of accused in the case Identify the document by its heading, cause title, case number, date and parties, not merely its database label or index reference.

Verification — Test this requirement: Where there is more than one accused, the Affidavit must state that no bail application has been moved by any co-accused and, if one has been moved, its details must give the Serial No. of the accused. Use Trigger Words only as locators; inspect supplied material and context before deciding. Read the complete relevant section and test every required element; a heading or conclusory assertion alone is insufficient.

Defect — Return Defect when applicability is clear and the available relevant evidence positively establishes: Where the number of accused is more than one, the affidavit fails to state that, no bail application has been moved by any of the co-accused persons and, if such an application has been moved, it's details fail to provide the Serial No. for the accused persons Apply this outcome only after the Legal-source gate has been satisfied; otherwise return Need Review. A complete relevant page/section suffices for a local defect despite unavailable unrelated material. Identify the document, page/section and decisive evidence.

Compliant — Return Compliant only when affirmative evidence establishes every element of the Requirement across its complete relevant scope. Apply this outcome only after the Legal-source gate has been satisfied; otherwise return Need Review.

Need Review — Return Need Review only for material uncertainty preventing this decision: necessary evidence is absent/illegible, applicability is unresolved, or controlling evidence conflicts. Inspect supplied material first; name the exact missing/conflicting evidence and why it is decisive. Do not claim a supplied excerpt is unavailable. Do not use Need Review because unrelated pages are missing, the whole file is unavailable, a keyword search failed, or relevant evidence already establishes Defect or Compliant. This is also the required result while the Legal-source gate remains unsatisfied.

N/A — Return N/A only when evidence affirmatively establishes that the filing is outside the petition/special-category scope or that a factual condition activating the Requirement does not arise. Missing evidence or uncertain applicability is not N/A.

Evidence — For D-292, record the document/page, applicability, decisive quote/visual observation, and any comparison or calculation. Do not infer facts.

defects.requirement: No application under Section 430 or 482 or 483 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023 for suspension of sentence and release on bail, grant of anticipatory bail or bail respectively shall be entertained unless it contains an averment that a similar application relating to the same subject matter has or has not been made to the Court.
defects.trigger_words: similar application; same subject matter; no similar application; earlier application; Section 430; Section 482; Section 483
where_to_look: Application: averment on a similar application on the same subject
Main Petition: averment on any similar earlier application
The numbered paragraph, often close to the "PRAYER", stating that "no similar application" on "the same subject matter" has been made, or that one has.
A valid averment says either way whether a similar application relating to the same subject matter was made to the Court.
The application under Section 430, 482 or 483 BNSS, or Sections 389, 438 or 439 CrPC, in this matter, as distinct from an application filed in the court below.
how_to_cure: 1. Disclosure of Earlier Similar Application

1.1. Prompt the User to confirm whether a similar application relating to the same subject matter has previously been made before the Court and, if so, provide the relevant details, with an option for Jubeex to fill the disclosure in the application.
1.2. Option for the User to add and edit the disclosure with Jubeex.
2. Particulars of Earlier Similar Application

2.1. Prompt the User to provide the prescribed particulars of the earlier similar application—Serial No., Name of Accused, Date of Application (if known), Case Number, Date of Order, and Bench, and option for Jubeex to fill the relevant portion of the application.
2.2. Option for the User to add and edit the particulars with Jubeex.

defects.notes:
Article 139A, Constitution of India:- 
(1) Where cases involving the same or
substantially the same questions of law are pending
before the Supreme Court and one or more High Courts
or before two or more High Courts and the Supreme
Court is satisfied on its own motion or on an application
made by the Attorney-General of India or by a party to
any such case that such questions are substantial
questions of general importance, the Supreme Court may
withdraw the case or cases pending before the High Court
or the High Courts and dispose of all the cases itself:
Provided that the Supreme Court may after
determining the said questions of law return any case so
withdrawn together with a copy of its judgment on such
questions to the High Court from which the case has
been withdrawn, and the High Court shall on receipt
thereof, proceed to dispose of the case in conformity
with such judgment.

defects.notes:
Article 139A, Constitution of India:- 
(1) Where cases involving the same or
substantially the same questions of law are pending
before the Supreme Court and one or more High Courts
or before two or more High Courts and the Supreme
Court is satisfied on its own motion or on an application
made by the Attorney-General of India or by a party to
any such case that such questions are substantial
questions of general importance, the Supreme Court may
withdraw the case or cases pending before the High Court
or the High Courts and dispose of all the cases itself:
Provided that the Supreme Court may after
determining the said questions of law return any case so
withdrawn together with a copy of its judgment on such
questions to the High Court from which the case has
been withdrawn, and the High Court shall on receipt
thereof, proceed to dispose of the case in conformity
with such judgment.

defects.defect: The petition has not been filed within the prescribed period of limitation.
defects.requirement: The applicable limitation period must be determined from the governing statute or Supreme Court Rule for the identified proceeding. Compliance must be calculated using the legally relevant impugned-order date, certified-copy application and readiness dates where applicable, permitted exclusions, and authoritative Supreme Court Registry filing/refiling timestamps. Do not infer limitation from a generic period or from drafting dates in uploaded pleadings.
defects.trigger_words: Limitation; Delay; condonation of delay; Date of Impugned Order; within limitation; Date of Judgment
where_to_look: Main Petition, Cover Page, and Listing Proforma: identify the proceeding type, governing provision, impugned decision, and dates asserted by the filer.
Impugned Order: authoritative pronouncement or order date.

Supreme Court Registry filing and refiling history: authoritative initial filing and subsequent refiling timestamps.
The governing limitation provision and any pleaded exclusion, extension, or condonation application.
Return needs_review if the applicable period or any legally necessary date is missing, disputed, or available only from a non-authoritative drafting date.
